title: Mediastinal masses and compartments: anatomy, anterior 4 Ts, biomarkers and airway management
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 58 (The Mediastinum)
Shields General Thoracic Surgery 8e Ch 181 (Mediastinal Compartments and Masses)
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Thymomas and Thymic Carcinomas

steps.say: The mediastinum is anatomically partitioned into three distinct surgical compartments. The anterosuperior compartment lies anterior to the pericardium and great vessels. The middle compartment contains the heart, pericardium, and tracheal bifurcation. The posterior compartment occupies the bilateral paravertebral gutters along the spine.
steps.tx: Surgically, the mediastinum is divided into the **anterosuperior compartment** (prevascular space), the visceral **middle compartment**, and the **posterior compartment** (paravertebral sulci). Each space contains resident embryonic structures that give rise to distinct pathological neoplasms and benign cysts during adult life.

vis.caption: Radiographic compartment boundaries of the mediastinum on lateral chest imaging. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Lateral chest radiograph demonstrating anterior, middle, and posterior mediastinal compartments.

steps.say: Anterior mediastinal masses follow the classic 4 Ts clinical rule. These comprise Thymoma and thymic carcinoma, Teratoma and germ cell tumors, Thyroid retrosternal goiter, and Terrible lymphoma. Computed tomography with intravenous contrast characterizes tissue density, calcifications, and invasiveness.
steps.tx: The diagnostic differential of anterior masses follows the **4 Ts of anterior mediastinum**: **thymoma** (and thymic carcinoma), **teratoma** (and germ cell neoplasms), substernal **thyroid** goiter, and aggressive **lymphoma**. Contrast CT delineates capsule integrity, fat planes, and invasion into neighboring vascular structures.

rows: Heterogeneous mass with fat, calcium, and fluid
Continuous extension from cervical thyroid gland

steps.say: The middle mediastinum houses congenital cysts and vascular structures. Common lesions include bronchogenic cysts, pericardial cysts, and enteric duplication cysts, alongside reactive or granulomatous lymphadenopathy. Bronchogenic cysts arise near the tracheal carina and occasionally require resection for compression or infection.
steps.tx: The visceral **middle mediastinum** contains the pericardial sac, tracheobronchial tree, and major vascular trunks. Pathological masses here predominantly represent benign congenital cysts, notably subcarinal **bronchogenic cysts**, fluid-filled **pericardial cysts**, enteric duplications, and infectious or neoplastic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing localized compression.

left.title: Bronchogenic Cysts
points: Arise from anomalous foregut budding near carina
Lined by ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium
Present with cough, stridor, or recurrent secondary infection

right.title: Pericardial Cysts
points: Arise from failed fusion of pericardial coelomic spaces
Typically located at right cardiophrenic angle

steps.say: The posterior mediastinum is the primary location for neurogenic tumors. Peripheral nerve neoplasms like schwannomas and neurofibromas originate along the intercostal nerves. Sympathetic chain tumors such as ganglioneuromas, neuroblastomas, and paragangliomas occupy the paravertebral sulcus.
steps.tx: The **posterior mediastinum** within the paravertebral gutter is overwhelmingly dominated by **neurogenic tumors**. Intercostal nerve sheaths produce benign **schwannoma** and neurofibroma, whereas the **sympathetic chain** gives rise to ganglioneuroma, aggressive ganglioneuroblastoma, and pediatric neuroblastoma, often requiring specialized surgical evaluation and care.

rows: Adults (20 to 50 years); mostly benign, round masses
Children and young adults; sympathetic trunk origin

steps.say: Serum tumor biomarkers are mandatory before performing a biopsy of an anterior mass. Serum alpha-fetoprotein and beta-hCG must be measured in every patient. Elevated alpha-fetoprotein confirms a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, directing immediate care toward chemotherapy rather than upfront surgical resection.
steps.tx: Mandatory evaluation before any invasive biopsy requires measuring **germ cell tumor markers**. Markedly elevated **alpha-fetoprotein** definitively establishes a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, while **beta-hCG** is elevated in choriocarcinoma and embryonal carcinoma, directing treatment toward upfront induction chemotherapy rather than early surgery.

nodes.label: Identify anterior mediastinal mass on chest CT
Measure serum AFP, beta-hCG, and LDH prior to biopsy
Initiate upfront cisplatin-based chemotherapy (avoid early resection)

steps.say: Pure seminoma presents with normal alpha-fetoprotein levels. Ten percent of pure seminomas exhibit a modest elevation in beta-hCG, but alpha-fetoprotein is never elevated. Any elevation in alpha-fetoprotein proves the existence of non-seminomatous elements and alters the therapeutic pathway.
steps.tx: A **pure seminoma** may present with a modest elevation of beta-hCG in up to 10 percent of cases, but **normal AFP** is strictly mandatory. Detection of any elevated alpha-fetoprotein confirms a non-seminomatous element, ruling out pure seminoma and mandating intensive **upfront chemotherapy** regimens.

left.title: Mediastinal Seminoma
points: Beta-hCG elevated in only 10% of cases
Extremely sensitive to cisplatin chemotherapy and radiation

right.title: Non-Seminomatous GCT
points: AFP frequently markedly elevated (yolk sac element)
Requires induction chemotherapy; residual mass resected

steps.say: Posterior neurogenic tumors can track into the spinal canal through neural foramina. This produces a characteristic dumbbell or hourglass configuration on magnetic resonance imaging. Resection requires a coordinated single-stage procedure combining neurosurgical laminectomy and thoracic surgical excision.
steps.tx: Posterior neurogenic tumors with **intraspinal extension** form a classic **dumbbell tumor** crossing the intervertebral neural foramen. Preoperative contrast-enhanced MRI of the spine is mandatory, followed by a coordinated single-stage **combined laminectomy-thoracotomy** to safely mobilize the intraspinal canal component before complete thoracic tumor resection.

nodes.label: Posterior mediastinal mass adjacent to neural foramen on CT
Perform contrast-enhanced MRI of spine to evaluate canal
Neurosurgical team performs laminectomy and mobilizes tumor
Thoracic team completes VATS or thoracotomy en-bloc excision

steps.say: Large anterior masses can cause catastrophic airway collapse during general anesthesia. Muscle relaxation and positive pressure ventilation abolish the negative pleural pressure that keeps compressed airways patent. Manage high-risk patients with awake fiberoptic intubation and maintain standby venoarterial ECMO.
steps.tx: Anesthesia in patients with a large **anterior mediastinal mass** carries severe risk of fatal **airway collapse** and right ventricular inflow occlusion upon induction. Loss of spontaneous negative pleural pressure causes sudden tracheal compression, requiring **awake intubation**, semi-fowler positioning, or standby **ECMO standby**.
